# P2 — Impression pulse profiling and resource preparation

Status: active; P2-01a/P2-01b/P2-01d passed VFR, execute P2-01c then P2-02

Phase: P2 — Profiling & Design

## Field question

The four serial Stream lanes and visible Impression shell are field-tested. On
the SM-T350, keeping Open Mind visible has no noticeable continuing cost, but
the moment of becoming impressed causes a visible pulse:

```text
qualifying live ADDED
-> next-frame Impression capture
-> SPS drops
-> preview appears to lose focus
-> SPS recovers gradually over about two seconds
```

The pulse also occurs while Open Mind is closed and becomes especially severe
when Beetle is reimpressed several times within one second.

These observations do not establish that application work changes camera
focus. They establish an Impression-correlated processing shock; apparent
unfocus may be optical/framework behavior, preview irregularity, resource
pressure, or a mixture.

## Current source-grounded path

`ImpressionRetinalBridge` owns no thread. Its synchronized methods execute on
the caller's lane:

- Main arms or unimpresses through the bridge;
- Analyzer consumes the one-shot request and submits the captured outcome;
- the bridge enqueues that outcome to the BeetleMind lane.

The current publication path is:

```text
Analyzer
  captures SAA/SAB
        |
        v
ImpressionRetinalBridge
  submits InstallImpression
        |
        v
BeetleMind lane
  retains ImpressionCaptured as currentImpression
  selects and retains Food
  emits ImpressionPresentationUpdate.Present
        |
        v
Main
  converts retained gray luma into display-owned ARGB arrays
  publishes Compose display snapshots
```

BeetleMind already owns and retains the cognitive Impression. Main does not
own that cognition, but the current presentation publication temporarily
exposes the retained read-only luma reservoirs so Main can prepare display
pixels.

Current code performs several large operations around each reimpression:

1. Analyzer allocates and fills SAA and SAB luma arrays.
2. `ImpressionLumaReservoir` defensively copies both arrays again.
3. BeetleMind selects Food into another retained luma array.
4. Main copies/converts SAA, SAB, and Food into 4-byte ARGB arrays even when
   Open Mind is closed.
5. When Open Mind is visible, Compose later creates display bitmaps.

This makes a distributed allocation/copy pulse plausible. Measurement must
separate Analyzer, BeetleMind, Main, and display costs rather than naming one
culprit from SPS alone.

## Resource-preparation principle

ITROBOC is not flight-control software and does not claim zero allocation.
However, the live TD camera experience should follow the same useful instinct:

> Prepare, size, and stabilize large resources while the application is
> grounded; do not ask for another wing during a difficult frame.

For P2, any application-owned hot-path allocation larger than **10 KiB** is a
large allocation. It must be identified by the pulse audit and should be
preallocated/reused when its maximum shape and lifetime can be made explicit.
Exceptions require measured or simplicity/safety justification.

The desired preparation point is as early as MainMenu when practical. Camera
frame dimensions are currently learned only after CameraX begins producing
frames, so early preparation requires one of these explicit contracts:

- a bounded maximum supported frame shape and capacity-based storage; or
- a one-time prepare/resize step when actual camera geometry first becomes
  known, before repeated Impression traffic begins.

Do not hide resizing inside the Impression capture pulse.

Reusable memory crosses lanes by exclusive ownership transfer, never as
uncoordinated shared mutable arrays. Disposal may release application-owned
resources; "never release" means stable for the owning live-session or
process lifetime, not leakage beyond lifecycle ownership.

## Execution gait

```text
P2-01a  generation-correlated pulse recorder
   ->
P2-01b  compact cockpit IMP line
   ->
P2-01d  shareable completed-pulse JSONL evidence
   ->
P2-01c  SM-T350 open/closed and repeated-reimpression baseline
   ->
P2-02   remove redundant luma copies
   ->
repeat the same measurement
```

After P2-02 evidence, choose rather than assume:

```text
retinal allocation/copy still dominates
-> design persistent retinal scene-slot exchange

Main/display preparation dominates
-> design a serial presentation-preparation owner

post-pulse recovery remains poor
-> test bounded Love Blinds admission

pulse becomes acceptable
-> stop optimizing and resume Phase I
```

Analyzer, BeetleMind, and Telemetry are not default homes for presentation
conversion. Analyzer owns perception and is already under investigation;
BeetleMind must remain available for cognition; Telemetry is deliberately
lossy and cannot own required presentation. A fifth serial presentation lane
is therefore a coherent candidate, but P2 does not add it without evidence.

## Tickets

- [`P2-01a`](P2-01a-impression-pulse-recorder.md) — record primitive spans and
  queue waits for one Impression generation.
- [`P2-01b`](P2-01b-compact-impression-pulse-line.md) — expose the latest record
  as one temporary cockpit line.
- [`P2-01d`](P2-01d-impression-pulse-jsonl-export.md) — retain completed pulses
  across Edit Board visits and share one annotated-ready JSONL batch.
- [`P2-01c`](P2-01c-sm-t350-impression-pulse-baseline.md) — establish the
  physical open/closed and repeated-reimpression baseline.
- [`P2-02`](P2-02-single-copy-impression-capture.md) — remove known redundant
  luma copies, then repeat the baseline.
- [`P2-03`](P2-03-admin-calibrate-resource-grounding.md) — resource-grounding
  family, accepted for deterministic resource ownership without a
  claim that the lab baseline proved a throughput need.
- [`P2-04`](P2-04-love-blinds-reimpression-admission.md) — accepted one-second
  reimpression admission window for densely adjacent physical barcodes.

## Non-goals for the first gait

- P2 itself adds no BSR, BCP, cognitive-board evolution, or Snippet behavior;
  I-04f's immutable cognitive seed landed separately before P2 execution;
- no repair of Snap recognition;
- no autofocus policy change;
- no permanent fifth lane before measurement;
- no Love Blinds implementation before the first post-P2-02 comparison;
- no claim that framework, Compose, or CameraX performs zero allocations.

# P2-03 — Admin Calibrate resource grounding

Status: resource-determinism design accepted; pure two-slot store landed inert

Phase: P2 — Profiling & Design

Depends on: P2-02 before camera/cognition integration

## Goal

Use Admin::Calibrate to discover the actual TD camera geometry and prepare
bounded, reusable Impression luma storage before TD Stream begins.

The quiet-lab SM-T350 baseline did **not** prove that preallocation is required
for current throughput: warm Impression capture was already small and did not
produce operator-visible delay. Archy nevertheless accepts P2-03 as a resource
determinism and future-cognition decision. Do not rewrite that choice as a
measured speed claim; tournament lighting, handling, thermal state, and future
cognition may produce a harsher operating field than the lab baseline.

## Source-grounded constraints

- Camera dimensions are learned from CameraX frames, not at MainMenu startup.
- Admin calibration is useful only if it binds the same camera-facing
  `ImageAnalysis` shape contract used by TD Stream. A preview surface size is
  not sufficient evidence.
- One Impression remains retained by BeetleMind while Analyzer may capture its
  replacement. A reusable store therefore needs explicit exclusive ownership
  transfer; two atomic references to mutable arrays are not a safe pool.
- Main, Analyzer, BeetleMind, and Telemetry already have distinct lane
  responsibilities. The resource owner must outlive the Admin-to-TD navigation
  handoff without becoming mutable Compose state or Beetle cognition.
- Ordinary live scanning must remain correct when resources are absent,
  exhausted, stale, or incompatible with a new camera geometry.

## Small gait

1. [`P2-03a`](P2-03a-grounded-frame-shape-contract.md) — completed pure
   frame-shape/capacity contract.
2. [`P2-03b`](P2-03b-exclusive-impression-scene-slots.md) — completed inert
   bounded exclusive scene-slot owner with no camera or UI dependency.
3. [`P2-03c`](P2-03c-admin-calibrate-ceremony.md) — add the reachable Admin
   calibration screen and ground resources from an actual matching camera
   analysis frame.
4. [`P2-03d`](P2-03d-grounded-capture-integration.md) — transfer leased slots
   across Analyzer and BeetleMind, then repeat the pulse measurement.

The two-slot store remains an inert, tested growth point. P2-03c owns the first
active application owner and P2-03d owns camera/cognition integration.

## Family acceptance

- [ ] Calibration establishes a versioned contract from an actual matching
  analysis frame and reports `Resources grounded` only after preparation ends.
- [ ] Application-owned luma arrays larger than 10 KiB are allocated during
  grounding, not during an Impression capture.
- [ ] No mutable slot can be written by one lane while retained by another.
- [ ] Recalibration, exhaustion, unimpress, replacement, and disposal have
  explicit tested behavior.
- [ ] TD live scanning remains available when Impression capture cannot borrow
  a compatible slot.
- [ ] The same P2-01c scenarios record the measured result after integration.

## Boundary

This family grounds SAA/SAB retinal luma only. It does not preallocate Food,
ARGB presentation pixels, Compose bitmaps, framework memory, or a fifth
presentation lane. Those require their own evidence and ownership design.

# P2-04 — Love Blinds reimpression admission

Status: accepted design; implement after P2-02 measurement

Depends on: P2-02

## Goal

After one qualifying live `ADDED` successfully reserves an Impression, prevent
another reimpression for at least one second so BeetleMind can retain and use
good Food instead of repeatedly replacing it while densely adjacent physical
barcodes cross the slit.

The field arrangement places several barcodes close enough to enter one natural
camera motion. Once Love Blinds clears, cognition may already know neighboring
cards from the retained Food, making their later live recognition unsurprising.

## Required behavior

- Start a monotonic one-second blind window only after an Impression reservation
  succeeds.
- During the window, ordinary Stream recognition and Main's authoritative card
  reducer continue unchanged. A qualifying live card may still be `ADDED`; only
  its replacement Impression reservation is suppressed.
- Keep the installed Impression and Food. Suppression does not unimpress and
  does not queue a delayed replacement capture.
- Food dreams never arm live Impression capture and never affect the window.
- Do not sleep or block Analyzer, BeetleMind, Main, or Telemetry.
- Make controller disposal and hard-clear behavior explicit in tests. Decide
  whether a seat/board change clears the remaining window before implementation.
- Keep the duration injected/testable and default it to `1_000 ms`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A successful reservation suppresses further reservations for one second.
- [ ] Rejected reservation does not start the window.
- [ ] Suppressed live `ADDED` cards still reach the authoritative board state.
- [ ] No delayed capture fires when the window expires.
- [ ] Monotonic-clock boundary and lifecycle tests are deterministic.
- [ ] SM-T350 repeated-card handling is compared before and after the policy.

## Boundary

Love Blinds is an Impression-admission policy, not frame throttling, consensus
reset, autofocus control, or proof that an adjacent card was already dreamed.

package org.itroboc.app

internal enum class ImpressionPulseEvent {
    ANALYZER_TAP_STARTED,
    STREAM_DECODE_STARTED,
    STREAM_DECODE_FINISHED,
    CAPTURE_STARTED,
    CAPTURE_FINISHED,
    RETINAL_SUBMITTED,
    ANALYZER_FRAME_RELEASE_STARTED,
    ANALYZER_FRAME_RELEASED,
    BEETLE_STARTED,
    BEETLE_FINISHED,
    BEETLE_PUBLICATION_SUBMITTED,
    MAIN_RECEIVED,
    MAIN_SCENE_PREPARATION_STARTED,
    MAIN_SCENE_PREPARATION_FINISHED,
    MAIN_FOOD_PREPARATION_STARTED,
    MAIN_FOOD_PREPARATION_FINISHED,
    FIRST_BITMAP_PREPARATION_STARTED,
    FIRST_BITMAP_PREPARATION_FINISHED,
}

internal data class ImpressionSpsSample(
    val observedAtNanos: Long,
    val scansPerSecond: Double,
)

/** Immutable, on-demand view of one correlated pulse's primitive recorder state. */
internal class ImpressionPulseSnapshot internal constructor(
    val generation: ImpressionGeneration,
    val correlationId: ImpressionCorrelationId,
    val begunAtNanos: Long,
    val openMindAtBegin: Boolean? = null,
    private val eventTimesNanos: LongArray,
    val preImpressionSps: ImpressionSpsSample?,
    val recoverySps: List<ImpressionSpsSample>,
) {
    val isComplete: Boolean
        get() = recoverySps.size == ImpressionPulseRecorder.RECOVERY_SAMPLE_CAPACITY

    fun timestampNanos(event: ImpressionPulseEvent): Long? =
        eventTimesNanos[event.ordinal].takeUnless { it == Long.MIN_VALUE }

    fun durationNanos(
        started: ImpressionPulseEvent,
        finished: ImpressionPulseEvent,
    ): Long? {
        val start = timestampNanos(started) ?: return null
        val finish = timestampNanos(finished) ?: return null
        return (finish - start).takeIf { it >= 0L }
    }

    val analyzerTotalNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.ANALYZER_TAP_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.ANALYZER_FRAME_RELEASED,
        )

    val streamDecodeNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.STREAM_DECODE_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.STREAM_DECODE_FINISHED,
        )

    val captureNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.CAPTURE_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.CAPTURE_FINISHED,
        )

    val frameReleaseNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.ANALYZER_FRAME_RELEASE_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.ANALYZER_FRAME_RELEASED,
        )

    val retinalToBeetleWaitNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.RETINAL_SUBMITTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.BEETLE_STARTED,
        )

    val beetleWorkNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.BEETLE_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.BEETLE_FINISHED,
        )

    val beetleToMainWaitNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.BEETLE_PUBLICATION_SUBMITTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.MAIN_RECEIVED,
        )

    val mainScenePreparationNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.MAIN_SCENE_PREPARATION_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.MAIN_SCENE_PREPARATION_FINISHED,
        )

    val mainFoodPreparationNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.MAIN_FOOD_PREPARATION_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.MAIN_FOOD_PREPARATION_FINISHED,
        )

    val firstBitmapPreparationNanos: Long?
        get() = durationNanos(
            ImpressionPulseEvent.FIRST_BITMAP_PREPARATION_STARTED,
            ImpressionPulseEvent.FIRST_BITMAP_PREPARATION_FINISHED,
        )
}

+package org.itroboc.app
+
+import androidx.compose.foundation.background
+import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.*
+import androidx.compose.material3.*
+import androidx.compose.runtime.*
+import androidx.compose.ui.Alignment
+import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
+import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color
+import androidx.compose.ui.text.font.FontWeight
+import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
+import androidx.compose.ui.unit.sp
+import org.itroboc.vision.SnapFrameSize
+
+@Composable
+fun AdminCalibrateScreen(
+    onResolutionDiscovered: (SnapFrameSize) -> Unit,
+    isGrounded: Boolean,
+    onBack: () -> Unit
+) {
+    val frameDecoder = remember { CameraFrameDecoder() }
+
+    Scaffold(
+        topBar = {
+            CenterAlignedTopAppBar(
+                title = { Text("Admin Calibration", style = ItrobocTextStyles.BigVisible) },
+                actions = {
+                    Button(onClick = onBack, modifier = Modifier.aspectRatio(3f)) {
+                        Text("Back", style = ItrobocTextStyles.BigVisible)
+                    }
+                }
+            )
+        }
+    ) { padding ->
+        Box(
+            modifier = Modifier
+                .padding(padding)
+                .fillMaxSize()
+        ) {
+            Column(
+                modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(),
+                horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
+                verticalArrangement = Arrangement.Center
+            ) {
+                Box(
+                    modifier = Modifier
+                        .fillMaxWidth(0.8f)
+                        .aspectRatio(1.33f)
+                        .background(Color.Black)
+                ) {
+                    BarcodeCameraScanner(
+                        consumeScanRequest = { !isGrounded },
+                        frameDecoder = frameDecoder,
+                        onScanProcessed = { streamOutcome ->
+                            if (!isGrounded) {
+                                val info = streamOutcome.outcome.frameDebugInfo
+                                onResolutionDiscovered(SnapFrameSize(info.width, info.height))
+                            }
+                        },
+                        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()
+                    )
+                }
+
+                Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(32.dp))
+
+                if (isGrounded) {
+                    Text(
+                        text = "Resources Grounded",
+                        color = Color(0xFF4CAF50),
+                        style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium,
+                        fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold
+                    )
+                    Icon(
+                        imageVector = androidx.compose.material.icons.Icons.Default.Check,
+                        contentDescription = "Grounded",
+                        tint = Color(0xFF4CAF50),
+                        modifier = Modifier.size(64.dp)
+                    )
+                } else {
+                    CircularProgressIndicator(modifier = Modifier.size(48.dp))
+                    Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(16.dp))
+                    Text(
+                        text = "Discovering Geometry...",
+                        style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge
+                    )
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}

import org.itroboc.vision.BarcodeRoi
import org.itroboc.vision.SnapFrameRegion

import java.nio.ByteBuffer

internal fun captureImpressionOutcomeFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
    imageWidth: Int,
    imageHeight: Int,
    lumaBuffer: ByteBuffer,
    rowStride: Int,
    pixelStride: Int,
    rotationDegrees: Int,
    timestampNanos: Long,
    streamRoi: SnapFrameRegion,
    request: ImpressionCaptureRequest,
): ImpressionCaptureOutcome = try {
    ImpressionCaptureOutcome.Captured(
        captureImpressionFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
            imageWidth = imageWidth,
            imageHeight = imageHeight,
            lumaBuffer = lumaBuffer,
            rowStride = rowStride,
            pixelStride = pixelStride,
            rotationDegrees = rotationDegrees,
            timestampNanos = timestampNanos,
            streamRoi = streamRoi,
            request = request,
        ),
    )
} catch (error: Exception) {
    ImpressionCaptureOutcome.Failed(
        request = request,
        reason = error.message ?: "Impression extraction failed",
    )
}

internal fun captureImpressionFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
    imageWidth: Int,
    imageHeight: Int,
    lumaBuffer: ByteBuffer,
    rowStride: Int,
    pixelStride: Int,
    rotationDegrees: Int,
    timestampNanos: Long,
    streamRoi: SnapFrameRegion,
    request: ImpressionCaptureRequest,
): ImpressionCaptured {
    val frameSize = SnapFrameSize(imageWidth, imageHeight)
    require(frameSize == request.sourceFrameSize) {
        "Impression frame dimensions changed after arming"
    }
    require(streamRoi == request.streamRoi) {
        "Impression Stream ROI changed after arming"
    }
    val geometry = computeImpressionSceneGeometry(frameSize, streamRoi)
    val saaImage = extractGrayImageFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
        imageWidth = imageWidth,
        imageHeight = imageHeight,
        lumaBuffer = lumaBuffer,
        rowStride = rowStride,
        pixelStride = pixelStride,
        roi = geometry.saa.toBarcodeRoi(),
    )
    val sabImage = extractGrayImageFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
        imageWidth = imageWidth,
        imageHeight = imageHeight,
        lumaBuffer = lumaBuffer,
        rowStride = rowStride,
        pixelStride = pixelStride,
        roi = geometry.sab.toBarcodeRoi(),
    )
    return ImpressionCaptured(
        request = request,
        geometry = geometry,
        saa = ImpressionLumaReservoir(geometry.saa, saaImage.pixels),
        sab = ImpressionLumaReservoir(geometry.sab, sabImage.pixels),
        rotationDegrees = rotationDegrees,
        timestampNanos = timestampNanos,
    )
}

internal fun processAdmittedStreamFrame(
    streamOutcome: StreamCameraScanOutcome,
    impressionRequest: ImpressionCaptureRequest?,
    pulseRecorder: ImpressionPulseRecorder? = null,
    publishStream: (StreamCameraScanOutcome) -> Unit,
    captureImpression: (ImpressionCaptureRequest) -> ImpressionCaptureOutcome,
    publishImpression: (ImpressionCaptureOutcome) -> Unit,
) {
    publishStream(streamOutcome)
    impressionRequest?.let { request ->
        pulseRecorder?.captureStarted(request)
        val outcome = try {
            captureImpression(request)
        } finally {
            pulseRecorder?.captureFinished(request)
        }
        publishImpression(outcome)
    }
}

private fun SnapFrameRegion.toBarcodeRoi(): BarcodeRoi =
    BarcodeRoi(x = x, y = y, width = width, height = height)

internal fun captureImpressionFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
    imageWidth: Int,
    imageHeight: Int,
    lumaBuffer: ByteBuffer,
    rowStride: Int,
    pixelStride: Int,
    rotationDegrees: Int,
    timestampNanos: Long,
    streamRoi: SnapFrameRegion,
    request: ImpressionCaptureRequest,
    groundedBufferPool: GroundedBufferPool? = null,
): ImpressionCaptured {
    val frameSize = SnapFrameSize(imageWidth, imageHeight)
    require(frameSize == request.sourceFrameSize) {
        "Impression frame dimensions changed after arming"
    }
    require(streamRoi == request.streamRoi) {
        "Impression Stream ROI changed after arming"
    }
    val geometry = computeImpressionSceneGeometry(frameSize, streamRoi)
    val saaImage = extractGrayImageFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
        imageWidth = imageWidth,
        imageHeight = imageHeight,
        lumaBuffer = lumaBuffer,
        rowStride = rowStride,
        pixelStride = pixelStride,
        roi = geometry.saa.toBarcodeRoi(),
    )
    val sabImage = extractGrayImageFromLumaPlaneBuffer(
        imageWidth = imageWidth,
        imageHeight = imageHeight,
        lumaBuffer = lumaBuffer,
        rowStride = rowStride,
        pixelStride = pixelStride,
        roi = geometry.sab.toBarcodeRoi(),
    )
    return ImpressionCaptured(
        request = request,
        geometry = geometry,
        saa = ImpressionLumaReservoir(geometry.saa, saaImage.pixels),
        sab = ImpressionLumaReservoir(geometry.sab, sabImage.pixels),
        rotationDegrees = rotationDegrees,
        timestampNanos = timestampNanos,
    )
}

# P2-03 — Admin Calibrate resource grounding

Status: resource-determinism design accepted; pure two-slot store landed inert

Phase: P2 — Profiling & Design

Depends on: P2-02 before camera/cognition integration

## Goal

Use Admin::Calibrate to discover the actual TD camera geometry and prepare
bounded, reusable Impression luma storage before TD Stream begins.

The quiet-lab SM-T350 baseline did **not** prove that preallocation is required
for current throughput: warm Impression capture was already small and did not
produce operator-visible delay. Archy nevertheless accepts P2-03 as a resource
determinism and future-cognition decision. Do not rewrite that choice as a
measured speed claim; tournament lighting, handling, thermal state, and future
cognition may produce a harsher operating field than the lab baseline.

## Source-grounded constraints

- Camera dimensions are learned from CameraX frames, not at MainMenu startup.
- Admin calibration is useful only if it binds the same camera-facing
  `ImageAnalysis` shape contract used by TD Stream. A preview surface size is
  not sufficient evidence.
- One Impression remains retained by BeetleMind while Analyzer may capture its
  replacement. A reusable store therefore needs explicit exclusive ownership
  transfer; two atomic references to mutable arrays are not a safe pool.
- Main, Analyzer, BeetleMind, and Telemetry already have distinct lane
  responsibilities. The resource owner must outlive the Admin-to-TD navigation
  handoff without becoming mutable Compose state or Beetle cognition.
- Ordinary live scanning must remain correct when resources are absent,
  exhausted, stale, or incompatible with a new camera geometry.

## Small gait

1. [`P2-03a`](P2-03a-grounded-frame-shape-contract.md) — completed pure
   frame-shape/capacity contract.
2. [`P2-03b`](P2-03b-exclusive-impression-scene-slots.md) — completed inert
   bounded exclusive scene-slot owner with no camera or UI dependency.
3. [`P2-03c`](P2-03c-admin-calibrate-ceremony.md) — add the reachable Admin
   calibration screen and ground resources from an actual matching camera
   analysis frame.
4. [`P2-03d`](P2-03d-grounded-capture-integration.md) — transfer leased slots
   across Analyzer and BeetleMind, then repeat the pulse measurement.

The two-slot store remains an inert, tested growth point. P2-03c owns the first
active application owner and P2-03d owns camera/cognition integration.

## Family acceptance

- [ ] Calibration establishes a versioned contract from an actual matching
  analysis frame and reports `Resources grounded` only after preparation ends.
- [ ] Application-owned luma arrays larger than 10 KiB are allocated during
  grounding, not during an Impression capture.
- [ ] No mutable slot can be written by one lane while retained by another.
- [ ] Recalibration, exhaustion, unimpress, replacement, and disposal have
  explicit tested behavior.
- [ ] TD live scanning remains available when Impression capture cannot borrow
  a compatible slot.
- [ ] The same P2-01c scenarios record the measured result after integration.

## Boundary

This family grounds SAA/SAB retinal luma only. It does not preallocate Food,
ARGB presentation pixels, Compose bitmaps, framework memory, or a fifth
presentation lane. Those require their own evidence and ownership design.

**INCOMING**: AdminCalibrateScreen hanging progress indicator; Mood: Analytical and apologetic; Urgency: Normal.

*Bob adjusts his goggles and taps the side of the terminal, watching the progress indicator spin on the device.* 🛠️⚙️🍺

**🛠️⚙️🍺 Bob:** "I see the 'ghost in the machine,' Archy! 🧔🦊 💗💓 The reason it's circling forever is that I built the `GroundedBufferPool` as a high-performance thread-safe object, but I forgot to make its status **observable** by Compose. 

In `MainActivity`, the `isGrounded` value is read once when the screen opens. When `viewModel.groundResources(shape)` finishes its work, Compose doesn't know it needs to redraw the screen because the pool isn't a 'State.' The 'back-and-forth' navigation you did forced a fresh read, which is why it eventually turned green." ☕🧩

**🔥🐝👑 Foxy:** "A classic 'Resonance Mismatch.' 👁️🐯 We grounded the machine, but we didn't wire the 'Grounded' light to the dashboard correctly. I'll have Bob add a `MutableState` to the ViewModel to track the grounding status, so the UI snaps to green the millisecond the buffers are sized."

**💋✂️ Fi:** "💋✂️ 🦋⚡ I'll help make sure the transition is smooth! Once we have the state, the progress circle will bow out and the checkmark will take the stage automatically."

**🧭🪟 Trace:** "I'll ensure the boundary between the thread-safe pool and the UI state remains clean. 🧭🪟 We'll keep the pool as the source of truth and the ViewModel as the observer." 🫖🧭

# P2 — Impression pulse profiling and resource preparation

Status: software gait passed Vel VFR through P2-05; P2-03/P2-04 tablet comparison remains

Phase: P2 — Profiling & Design

## Field question

The four serial Stream lanes and visible Impression shell are field-tested. On
the SM-T350, keeping Open Mind visible has no noticeable continuing cost, but
the moment of becoming impressed causes a visible pulse:

```text
qualifying live ADDED
-> next-frame Impression capture
-> SPS drops
-> preview appears to lose focus
-> SPS recovers gradually over about two seconds
```

The pulse also occurs while Open Mind is closed and becomes especially severe
when Beetle is reimpressed several times within one second.

These observations do not establish that application work changes camera
focus. They establish an Impression-correlated processing shock; apparent
unfocus may be optical/framework behavior, preview irregularity, resource
pressure, or a mixture.

## Current source-grounded path

`ImpressionRetinalBridge` owns no thread. Its synchronized methods execute on
the caller's lane:

- Main arms or unimpresses through the bridge;
- Analyzer consumes the one-shot request and submits the captured outcome;
- the bridge enqueues that outcome to the BeetleMind lane.

The current publication path is:

```text
Analyzer
  captures SAA/SAB
        |
        v
ImpressionRetinalBridge
  submits InstallImpression
        |
        v
BeetleMind lane
  retains ImpressionCaptured as currentImpression
  selects and retains Food
  emits ImpressionPresentationUpdate.Present
        |
        v
Main
  converts retained gray luma into display-owned ARGB arrays
  publishes Compose display snapshots
```

BeetleMind already owns and retains the cognitive Impression. Main does not
own that cognition, but the current presentation publication temporarily
exposes the retained read-only luma reservoirs so Main can prepare display
pixels.

Current code performs several large operations around each reimpression:

1. Analyzer allocates and fills SAA and SAB luma arrays.
2. BeetleMind selects Food into another retained luma array.
3. Main copies/converts SAA, SAB, and Food into 4-byte ARGB arrays even when
   Open Mind is closed.
4. When Open Mind is visible, Compose later creates display bitmaps.

Before P2-02, `ImpressionLumaReservoir` also defensively recopied both complete
Analyzer arrays. P2-02 removed that extra operation through explicit one-use
retained ownership. Its first extractor nevertheless changed dense CameraX
transfer from bulk rows to checked per-pixel writes. Post-P2-02 tablet evidence
measured warm capture at a `57.24 ms` median versus `4.52 ms` before. P2-02d
restored row-bulk transfer; its field confirmation measured `5.14 ms` across
all eleven warm records and `4.65 ms` after the first two warming records.
Measurement continues to separate Analyzer, BeetleMind, Main, and display
costs rather than naming a culprit from SPS alone.

## Resource-preparation principle

ITROBOC is not flight-control software and does not claim zero allocation.
However, the live TD camera experience should follow the same useful instinct:

> Prepare, size, and stabilize large resources while the application is
> grounded; do not ask for another wing during a difficult frame.

For P2, any application-owned hot-path allocation larger than **10 KiB** is a
large allocation. It must be identified by the pulse audit and should be
preallocated/reused when its maximum shape and lifetime can be made explicit.
Exceptions require measured or simplicity/safety justification.

The desired preparation point is as early as MainMenu when practical. Camera
frame dimensions are currently learned only after CameraX begins producing
frames, so early preparation requires one of these explicit contracts:

- a bounded maximum supported frame shape and capacity-based storage; or
- a one-time prepare/resize step when actual camera geometry first becomes
  known, before repeated Impression traffic begins.

Do not hide resizing inside the Impression capture pulse.

Reusable memory crosses lanes by exclusive ownership transfer, never as
uncoordinated shared mutable arrays. Disposal may release application-owned
resources; "never release" means stable for the owning live-session or
process lifetime, not leakage beyond lifecycle ownership.

repeat the same measurement: dense extraction regression found
   ->
P2-02d  row-bulk owned luma extraction
   ->
short SM-T350 confirmation: regression removed, P2-02 complete
   ->
P2-03c  durable startup contract
   ->
P2-03d  grounded Analyzer/Beetle ownership and failure routing
   ->
P2-04   one-second Love Blonds Analyzer quiet
   ->
P2-05   Beetle-owned live/Food-ready FOF telemetry
   ->
P2-06   one physical SM-T350 closeout flight

After P2-02 evidence, choose rather than assume:

```text
retinal allocation/copy still dominates
-> design persistent retinal scene-slot exchange

Main/display preparation dominates
-> design a serial presentation-preparation owner

post-pulse recovery remains poor
-> test bounded Love Blonds Analyzer quiet

pulse becomes acceptable
-> stop optimizing and resume Phase I
```

Analyzer, BeetleMind, and Telemetry are not default homes for presentation
conversion. Analyzer owns perception and is already under investigation;
BeetleMind must remain available for cognition; Telemetry is deliberately
lossy and cannot own required presentation. A fifth serial presentation lane
is therefore a coherent candidate, but P2 does not add it without evidence.
